## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a production-ready 3D pixel-art survival horror/laboratory escape game titled “Ape Project” in the current repo, featuring a 15×15 m lab lobby with 4 hydraulic doors/switches, 500×500 m hilly sparse jungle, Lethal-Ape-style player, and blind acoustic predator “Mossman.”

## Requirements
- All world assets dynamically generated: 3D pixel-art lab, racks/beakers/terminals, hydraulic doors with left-side switches, hilly jungle trees, player animations (walk/sprint quadruped/crouch), 2.8 m eyeless moss-striped Mossman with 33 km/h speed, 50% turning resistance, acoustic tracking.
- No flat 2D sprite assets, rigid 8-bit restrictions, or modern realistic high-poly models.
- Include dynamic voxel-grid physics, atmospheric lighting/shaders, crisp pixel texture mapping, procedural animations/particles/AI.
- Must be playable and responsive, including desktop and mobile.
- User’s prompt was truncated after “hydraulic door a”; assistant inferred remaining intent rather than asking.

## Decisions
- Built with Vite + Three.js (`three@0.187.0`), vanilla JS modules, no external game assets.
- Internal render resolution capped at 960 px width with CSS nearest-neighbor pixelation; HUD rendered at native resolution.
- Added inferred objective loop: recover 3 jungle research cores, return to lab terminal to win; Mossman escalates after pickups.
- Lab is a true sanctuary that Mossman cannot enter; hydraulics are loud and attract him.
- Procedural WebAudio soundscape; audio starts on title-screen click gesture.
- Static lab and landmark meshes are batch-merged by material to reduce draw calls; dynamic doors, hologram, core rigs, beacon/fire remain separate.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repo initialized with `package.json`, Vite config, local fonts, full HTML/CSS HUD/title/map/end overlays.
- Implemented procedural textures in `src/textures.js`.
- Implemented lab geometry, 4 hydraulic doors, left-side switches, terminal, props, lighting and merging in `src/lab.js`.
- Implemented 500×500 terrain, paths, bunker exterior, merged forest/undergrowth/rocks, three landmarks and cores in `src/jungle.js`.
- Implemented player rig and locomotion/stamina/footstep/noise system in `src/player.js`.
- Implemented Mossman model, patrol/investigate/chase/search/lurk/attack AI, acoustic hearing and inertia in `src/mossman.js`.
- Implemented UI/compass/map/threat radar/toasts/end screens in `src/ui.js`.
- Implemented procedural audio in `src/audio.js`; voxel debris, sound waves, camera shake in `src/effects.js`.
- Implemented game orchestration, start/pause/map/win/death/reset, camera modes, flashlight, interactions in `src/main.js`.
- Production HTTP server runs via tmux session `ape` at `http://localhost:3002`.
- First title-screen screenshot captured successfully at `screenshots/title.png`; visually shows the lab, title lockup, directive, controls, and start button.

### Active
- Visual/performance QA and gameplay validation.
- Current title render reports 462 draw calls, 569 meshes, 581,529 triangles, 19 lights; software rendering is slow (~14 frames after several seconds), though screenshot now succeeds.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/title.png` and improve title composition/lighting if needed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a production-ready 3D pixel-art survival horror/laboratory escape game titled “Ape Project” in the current repo, featuring a 15×15 m lab lobby with 4 hydraulic doors/switches, 500×500 m hilly sparse jungle, Lethal-Ape-style player, and blind acoustic predator “Mossman.”

## Requirements
- All world assets dynamically generated: 3D pixel-art lab, racks/beakers/terminals, hydraulic doors with left-side switches, hilly jungle trees, player animations (walk/sprint quadruped/crouch), 2.8 m eyeless moss-striped Mossman with 33 km/h speed, 50% turning resistance, acoustic tracking.
- No flat 2D sprite assets, rigid 8-bit restrictions, or modern realistic high-poly models.
- Include dynamic voxel-grid physics, atmospheric lighting/shaders, crisp pixel texture mapping, procedural animations/particles/AI.
- Must be playable and responsive, including desktop and mobile.
- User’s prompt was truncated after “hydraulic door a”; assistant inferred remaining intent rather than asking.

## Decisions
- Built with Vite + Three.js (`three@0.187.0`), vanilla JS modules, no external game assets.
- Internal render resolution capped at 960 px width with CSS nearest-neighbor pixelation; HUD rendered at native resolution.
- Added inferred objective loop: recover 3 jungle research cores, return to lab terminal to win; Mossman escalates after pickups.
- Lab is a true sanctuary that Mossman cannot enter; hydraulics are loud and attract him.
- Procedural WebAudio soundscape; audio starts on title-screen click gesture.
- Static lab and landmark meshes batch-merged by material; door panels newly merged; transmission removed from glass to avoid a costly extra scene pass.
- Portrait/mobile uses wider shoulder-camera distance, 68° FOV, and a 3-column touch action grid.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repo initialized with `package.json`, Vite config, local fonts, full HTML/CSS HUD/title/map/end overlays.
- Implemented procedural textures, lab geometry, 4 hydraulic doors, left-side switches, terminal, props, lighting, static merging.
- Implemented 500×500 terrain, paths, bunker exterior, merged forest/undergrowth/rocks, three landmarks and cores.
- Implemented player rig, locomotion/stamina/footstep/noise, Mossman model/AI/acoustic tracking, UI, audio, particles, camera shake, game orchestration.
- Verified title screen, desktop lobby, hydraulic door opening/collider disable, outside zone transition, core collection (3/3), terminal win, restart, pause/resume, map open/close, death/retry.
- Verified Mossman chase reaches 9.17 m/s, attacks for 34 damage, and is blocked at lab threshold in `lurk` state.
- Verified mobile title layout, start, touch joystick movement, look-zone rotation, USE, MAP, LAMP, and pause buttons.
- Reduced draw calls from ~462–555 to ~214 title / ~288 playing via transmission removal and door merging; measured llvmpipe still ~1.7 fps.
- Fixed `UI.setMap` error `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cores')` by removing premature `drawMap()` call.
- Fixed mobile title clipping and moved mobile interaction prompt above touch controls.

### Active
- Final QA and visual polish across desktop/mobile.
- Performance tuning for software renderer (llvmpipe) and remaining runtime checks.
- Final production build verification and documentation.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Reload desktop/mobile after latest `ui.js` fix and re-open map to confirm zero console errors.
2. Capture final screenshots: desktop title/lobby/map/Mossman/jungle and mobile title/gameplay.
3. Test flashlight toggle, crouch/sprint animations, core interaction prompt from actual proximity, and touch USE near a door switch.
4. Run `npm run build` and verify production preview.
5. Optionally add a software-renderer low-quality mode (reduced terrain/forest resolution, fewer lights/shadows) if llvmpipe responsiveness matters.
6. Update `README.md` with controls and run instructions.
7. Review git status; all implementation remains uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game flow, input, camera, interactions, win/death/reset handling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/lab.js`: lab geometry, doors, switches, terminal, door/static merging.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/jungle.js`: terrain, forest, landmarks, cores, static detail merging.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: ape rig, movement, collision, animation, noise/footsteps.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/mossman.js`: predator model and acoustic AI states.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: HUD, compass, map, radar, overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: voxel debris, sound rings, camera shake.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: procedural canvas textures.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM/HUD/title/overlays/touch buttons.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles.css`: full UI/title/responsive/touch styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: QA screenshots incl. `title2.png`, `lobby2.png`, `door-open.png`, `win.png`, `death.png`, `map.png`, `mossman-model.png`, `mobile-title2.png`, `mobile-play2.png`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: scripts (`npm run dev`, `npm run build`).

## Important Context
- Vite server runs in tmux session `ape` at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright sessions `ape` (desktop) and `apem` (mobile) are active.
- `window.__APE_PROJECT__` exposes the live game; valid states: `boot`, `title`, `playing`, `paused`, `map`, `dead`, `won`.
- Chrome uses llvmpipe; measured ~1.7 fps desktop/title and ~2.7 fps at 480px with lights/shadows disabled, so real gameplay QA often requires manually stepping updates (`g.lab.update(dt)`, `g.mossman.update(...)`).
- Current calls/tris: ~214 calls / 348k tris on title, ~288 calls / 349k tris playing; transmission removal roughly halved calls and triangles.
- Player spawn is now `(0, 0, 3.5)` facing north; terminal interactable near `(0, 1, 2.8)`.
- Core anchors: watchtower ~`(-128, 83)`, crash site ~`(154, -105)`, shrine ~`(37, 184)`.
- Mossman spawn `(92, -74)`, chase speed `9.17 m/s`, blocked around lab footprint.
- Game title screen is intentionally shown before play; click `#start-btn` to begin.
- `Map` close must use `#map-close` on mobile; touch MAP button is behind overlay.
- Latest touch button IDs: `#btn-map`, `#btn-light` (not `#btn-lamp`), `#btn-pause`.
- All changes remain uncommitted in the working tree.

The entire game world—spanning a secure 15x15m subterranean laboratory lobby with interactive hydraulic security doors, an expansive 500x500m slightly hilly sparse jungle exterior, a Lethal-Ape-inspired agile player model, and the terrifying blind auditory apex predator \"Mossman\"—must be rendered strictly through high-fidelity 3D pixel-art engines combined with dynamic voxel-grid physics, atmospheric lighting shaders, and crisp pixel texture mapping, completely avoiding flat 2D sprites, rigid 8-bit retro restrictions, or modern high-poly realistic models. All visual assets, hydraulic pneumatic animations, particle trails, and creature AI behaviors are dynamically generated in real-time.
1. Laboratory Lobby @COMMENT_BODY@ Hydraulic Door Architecture (15x15M)
The Starting Sanctuary: Upon launching a new session, the player spawns securely inside a high-tech subterranean laboratory lobby measuring precisely 15x15 meters.
Interior Environment @COMMENT_BODY@ Assets: The room features grid-aligned metallic walls, industrial flooring, and detailed 3D pixel-art laboratory racks and storage shelving units lined with glass beakers, chemical containers, and computer terminals with crisp pixel textures.
4-Way Hydraulic Security System: Heavy, reinforced pneumatic hydraulic doors are embedded directly into the left, right, front, and back walls of the laboratory.
Interactive Left-Side Control Switches: Each door features a tactile mechanical control switch positioned precisely on the left side of the door frame. Players must manually interact with this switch to trigger the smooth, weighted hydraulic open and close cycle, controlling safe egress into the outside world.
2. Exterior Open-World Jungle Map (500x500M)
The Wilderness Expanse: Stepping past the laboratory doors leads directly into a massive, open-world jungle map measuring 500x500 meters in total scale.
Terrain Morphology @COMMENT_BODY@ Foliage: The landscape features slightly rolling, hilly terrain that creates natural elevation changes, valleys, and line-of-sight blockades, sparsely populated with scattered 3D pixel-art trees that provide open tracking fields mixed with tactical cover points.
3. Player Character Architecture @COMMENT_BODY@ Lethal-Ape Animation Framework
Player Model (Lethal Ape Style): A highly detailed, rugged 3D pixel-art ape character model directly inspired by the iconic movement mechanics and silhouette of Lethal Ape, rendered with clean, high-definition pixel texturing.
Animation @COMMENT_BODY@ Locomotion System: Features ultra-smooth pixel animation frames for quadrupedal sprinting, upright walking, fluid climbing over hilly terrain, crouching, and responsive first-person or third-person camera switching.
4. Apex Predator Ecosystem: The Mossman
The primary terror roaming the 500x500m outdoor jungle, hunting relentlessly through acoustic tracking:
Monster Designation: Mossman
Spawn Zone: Deployed natively across the outdoor jungle map.
Physical Morphology @COMMENT_BODY@ Appearance:
Height @COMMENT_BODY@ Build: A towering, muscular ape-like entity standing at 2.8 meters tall.
Color @COMMENT_BODY@ Texture: Covered in vibrant moss-green base skin intricately woven with dark green moss stripes winding across and around its entire massive body, styled with detailed pixel shading.
Facial Features: Completely eyeless (devoid of any optical organs or eyes), featuring only a wide, unsettlingly visible mouth stretching across its lower face.
Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Movement Metrics:
Top Movement Speed: Blistering fast at 33 KM/h.
Turning Agility @COMMENT_BODY@ Inertia: 50% turning difficulty/resistance, meaning the creature possesses realistic momentum and requires wide, sweeping arcs to change direction at top speed.
Sensory System @COMMENT_BODY@ Unique Abilities:
Acoustic Tracking: Completely blind to visual stimuli, but equipped with Super-Sensitive Hearing that instantly detects player footsteps, running ripples, and hydraulic door a
"
